data.name: Jivansh
data.long_meaning: Jivansh is a compound name, derived from the Sanskrit words ‘jiva’ meaning ‘living being’ and ‘ansh’ meaning ‘part’ or ‘soul’. This name is often used to denote the divine spark within each individual. In Hindu mythology, Jivansh is believed to be a part of the divine soul that is present in all living beings. This name is therefore deeply spiritual and carries a profound meaning.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of the divine soul within.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jivansh holds significant cultural importance in Hindu traditions, especially in the context of spiritual growth and personal development. It is often used as a reminder of the interconnectedness of all living beings and the importance of treating others with compassion and respect.
data.spiritual_significance: For Hindus, the name Jivansh holds deep spiritual significance as it represents the indwelling divine presence in all beings. It is believed that each individual possesses a jivatma, or indivisible soul, which is a part of the universal divine consciousness, or brahman. This belief encourages a sense of unity and interconnectedness among all living beings and highlights the importance of spiritual growth and self-realization.

historical_references.reference: Jivansh was a title given to the eighth Tirthankara, Mahavira. He is regarded as the founder of Jainism and lived around 599-527 BC.
historical_references.context: Religious leader and founder of Jainism

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Jivansh is found in the Hindu scripture, Mahabharata, where Jivansh is mentioned as a King and a descendant of Ikshvaku Dynasty. No exact time period is mentioned in the text.
historical_references.context: King and descendant of Ikshvaku Dynasty
